newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran tightens curbs on filmmakers. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iran tightens curbs on filmmakers. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]

text.p: Iran has tightened restrictions on Iranian film producers, saying they now needed official permission before they could sell international distribution rights to their films, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The English-language Iran News daily said the restrictions were announced in a statement by the Culture and Islamic Guidance Ministry.

"Iranian producers who intend to sell the international screening rights of their movies to foreign distributors are required to submit their relevant contracts for approval to the evaluation and screening department of the ministry," it quoted the statement as saying.
Films produced in the Islamic republic already need ministry approval before they could be produced or screened.

Film industry sources said the new curbs were introduced after the screening of two Iranian films at a festival in Jerusalem last month. Iran had denounced the screenings as a "plot hatched by Europe and the illegal state of Israel".

They said the films' director Mohsen Makhmalbaf had no knowledge that a French distribution company which bought the international rights to his films would show them in Israel -- a state that Iran believes has no right to exist.
Some Iranian films are being well received by international critics.
An Iranian film was jointly awarded the Golden Palm (corrects from Golden Globe) best film award at the Cannes film festival earlier this year.
Director Abbas Kiarostami's "The Taste of the Cherry" was a late entry after Iran's Foreign Ministry intervened to overturn a ban imposed by the Culture and Islamic Guidance Ministry.
He said then the ministry told him he would be banned from showing the film in Cannes because it should be shown first at a festival in Tehran.
